$PLTR quarter is one of those moments where operating reality & market imagination finally meet and the question is whether the imagination has gone too far.

I don't think people realize how insane it is to grow revenue 63% while maintaining 51% operating margins in software. That level of efficiency is almost unheard of which is why $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang called Palantir’s ontology “the most important enterprise stack in the world.”

The ratio of commercial revenue to customer count is just as extreme with only 530 commercial customers generating ~$400M in one quarter when most software companies at that revenue scale have thousands of clients so this is an insane ratio for enterprise software.

Every story you see about $GOOGL, $MSFT, $META, $AMZN, $ORCL or OpenAI building new compute factories feeds directly into why Palantir can post numbers like this. Palantir captures the software layer where that infrastructure spending turns capacity into productivity.

So yes, the stock trades rich but it’s also the only pure play with exposure to every hyperscaler dollar being spent. Palantir doesn’t buy GPUs or build datacenters since it simply benefits from everyone else’s CapEx.

Constellation Brands/ $STZ just filed an 8‑K noting a prospectus supplement for the resale of up to 21,274,829 Class A shares by named selling stockholders. STZ will not receive any proceeds from those sales"
My guess is Berkshire is going to buy one of the Sands Brothers out (or half of each). The Sands brothers own a lot of the stock (a little over 20m shares, worth about 2.6b each at $130. Robert used to be CEO). This sure looks like a cash out to me.

Not only that, I wouldn't be surprised if the large buy this morning was Weschler who I strongly believe intiated the position (see quote tweet). It would be pretty hard not to market buy there if you know Warren is about to buy a brother out at 140-150 or something (Weschler's cost basis is at least 200 i believe) and meanwhile people are market selling at $127. With 13fs coming up soon, if Weschler/Berkshire had been market buying already, they really would need to get this done before any jump in the price as well.

As a shareholder, the first thought is "am i about to get diluted?" no, this is just shares changing hands between existing owners. The problem is Berkshire should be buying the shares on the market which would make the price go up. However, as an STZ holder (unlike say, Palantir), you really want the stock price to go down as much as possible (i know, i know).

Almost no one at STZ is paid in stock. The company uses debt effectively and tries to maintain 2.5x debt/ebitda, which is pretty optimal for cannibals. The company buys back tonnes of shares. The best case scenario is a low stock price for a long time, but with great business performance. Then cash flow per share explodes. Eventually the stock must rerate (say 20 PE) and then management ideally does more dividends and less buybacks.

If Berkshire buys the 21m shares, they will own close to 20% of the company. Then Warren can leave it there to eat itself like he's done with Coca Cola. Modelo was first brewed in 1925 and is now the number 1 beer in America (which happened under the new CEO, so the transition in management has gone well). Like Coke, American Express and the Japanese Trading Companies, my read is he views this spot as +EV even if he's never allowed to sell a share again.

We shall see.

people act like the depreciation on GPUs is really difficult, so i made this simple guide.
you're the gpu maker: we've gone from a 2 year replacement cycle to an 18 month one, pump the stock pls.
you're a growth ceo talking to investors: those gpus last 12 years, lend us money pls.
you're the growth ceo talking to your CFO: depreciate those gpus as fast as possible, fuck paying taxes.
you're the investor shorting the stock: those gpus only last 2 years, look at what the CFO just said!
you're a mega cap CEO trying to protect your P/E ratio / bond rating, which is more important to you than tax optimization: those GPUs last 8 years
you're an investor longing the stock: those gpus last 8 years.
the reality: the GPUs probably last a little over 5 years but it is hard to tell if the data center capacity will be better used with new ones at that point especially considering the cost of power / the power efficiency of the new gpus.

Softbank ($9984/$SFTBY) has started selling the farm to buy more OpenAI. 9 billion of $ARM sold and counting.
Since writeup:
$9984: gone from 8000y to 23000, +187%.
$ARM: gone from $140 to $149.71: +7%.

Today, ARM -5% $SFTBY +3%.

Very good chance ARM actually goes below $140 which was the price at the start of the writeup, as Softbank has increased their margin account against the shares to $20 billion now. I assume they are dumping immediately.

People give Masa a lot of flack but his moves here have gone very well, whether by luck or design.
1. Borrowed shitloads of yen to buy US stocks. Yen continuing to devalue, US tech stocks continuing to go up.
2. Bought a bunch of NVDA, made a tonne on it. Locked in OAI calls at $300b market cap, then only bought once they had resold OAI equity >500b market cap.
3. Has managed to liquidate very significant amounts of $ARM without as much price devaluation as I expected.
4. Bought $INTC at $22ish, up a lot there.
5. Building a large robotics portfolio for the future.

I have maintained my initial position and actually increased a bit on the last dip, but chickened out and resold the last lots, so I am sitting comfortably at a little over 10% of net equity here.

As a side note, its hilarious to see all the $NVDA holders rooting against OAI when Anthropic and Google's success are putting $AMZN and $GOOG ASIC plans into overdrive. Who is left to buy the $NDVA chips? Just $META and OAI lol. You guys are keying your own car rooting against Sam. I get it, but if OAI goes down, $NVDA is going to be stressed big time in the short term. There's lots of LLM providers out there, I don't buy the argument that OAI is systemically important, but to NVDA they are hence the "gpus for 10% of your equity" deal.

People really want to attribute these things to one person, but the reality is that $GOOG has always had an extremely deep bench in AI but suffered from lacking a singular product vision.
Once you tell the whole company "We're doing AGI, end of story", and that seems like... doable? all the little teams start working much better together.
Noam Shazeer + Jeff Dean getting a small team back to the office to do the Manhattan Project thing https://t.co/KCa30HJuG1.
Sergey excited to be involved in something thats not ads.
Demis team at Deep Mind having their work productized.
Sundar making sure it all runs properly.

Once things started clicking, it became cool to be a Google dev again and you had the momentum on X etc.

The talent has always been there, there was just never a clear unifying vision for the company (which was probably optimal. you need a pretty big product to bet your conglomerate on it).

text:
Quick GTOPort Updates, Nov 22 2025.
1. Fixed a new bug for new accounts: i noticed that when you created a new account, the default portfolioview did not let you add positions manually. So if you wanted to have a manual only account (without importing data from your brokerage) this was impossible. I've fixed this now. I recommend giving the site another shot if this was your intended use.
2. Semi private portfolio sharing: Some users wanted the ability to share their portfolio publicly, but without $ figures, a semi-private view if you will. I've added this functionality (image 1). You can check out how that looks here: https://t.co/jnHMCjzI7s. I also added a channel on discord (https://t.co/AZod5FDDfc) where users can discuss their Ports now that there's the option for more privacy.
3. Multiple accounts at once: Multiple Interactive Brokers accounts can now be paired at once. I implemented this previously but since I didn't use multiple myself it was hard to make sure it worked. Now I do, and it does.
4. Japanese translation and financial data: Putting a lot of work into the Japanese features on GTOPort lately. Handling document translations is so much better than using doctranslator now, and i'm working on deploying a much more scaled solution so every filing is translated without waiting. If you are splitting up doctranslator files still and increasingly frustrated doing this, please join the discord and I will help you out: https://t.co/AZod5FDDfc.
5. Work on the GTOAgent continues.... stay tuned.

text:
Small feature update: Portfolio Notes.
Done an absolute tonne of work on https://t.co/yKPiGcmCsq lately to get all the financials data working for research. But took a little breather to KO this small feature request - adding notes to your portfolio.

The cool thing about notes in GTOPort is that each night, a timestamp of your portfolio is made. You can go back and forward in time very easily, to see whats changed. If you make a quick note of your thinking or thesis when you put a position on, then change the note later, you can always go back and see what you were thinking.

And since the GTOAgent has all your timestamped portfolio history, your notes will also be in-context when you chat to it about how to improve your trading, where your big mistakes were, etc.
